title: The Core Facilitator sets Sky Direct Exposure limits by Forum post, and those values supersede the Risk Framework
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.1 puts designation of Sky Direct Exposures with the Core Facilitator "in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor via posts to the Sky Forum under the 'Sky Core' category," recorded in Active Data the Core Facilitator maintains by Direct Edit.

A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.4 extends the same route to the parameters — rate limits and aggregate exposure limits — with initial values and updates posted to the same Forum category, and then adds the clause that matters: "The values for the parameters for Sky Direct Exposures are set by the Core Facilitator and **supersede any values for these parameters specified in the Risk Framework**."

So a Forum post by one office, after consultation with an advisor, overrides the ecosystem's Risk Framework for this class of exposure. No vote, no Atlas Edit cycle, no Facilitator-and-token-holder review of the kind that governs every Primitive Instance parameter elsewhere in this Article.

The justification is presumably speed and ownership: these are Sky's own positions, funded by Sky, with the Agent bearing no risk, so the party with the exposure sets its own limits and can adjust them as market conditions move. Requiring a governance cycle to change a Treasury Bill exposure limit would make the mechanism unusable.

The cost is that the Risk Framework — which binds Prime Agents strictly — is unilaterally displaceable for a growing list of asset classes by an actor whose decisions are recorded in a Forum thread. The Active Data lists provide traceability (each designation carries a date, and ended exposures move to a Previous list), but traceability is not the same as approval.
description: Rate limits and aggregate exposure limits are designated and updated via posts to the Sky Forum in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, overriding any Risk Framework values.
